subject: Recap + runbook: MedLytics isolation, ops MOP and SLA confirmation
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Marino <alicia@medlytics.com>; Tom Whitaker <tom@medlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + runbook: MedLytics isolation, ops MOP and SLA confirmation

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for making time this morning. Quick recap from our call and the proposed runbook so we have a single source of truth as we head into procurement and security review. I’ve attached the initial MOP (MedLytics-MOP-draft.pdf) — consider it a working draft.

Key pain points you called out:
- Strict data isolation for PHI workflows (no co-tenant access).
- Predictable latency for inference on clinical prompts (p95 target).
- Smooth scale-up during batch/overnight ingest without cold-start penalties.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Provision a dedicated, single-tenant GPU pool for production inference (isolated VPC with customer-managed peering).
2) Hit SLA target of 99.9% monthly uptime and p95 generation latency < 150 ms for typical patient-summary calls (we discussed tightening to 120ms if benchmarks allow).
3) Support autoscaling + warm pool to avoid cold-starts; burst capacity available for weekly batch jobs.
4) Multi-region DR: primary in us-west, failover to us-east with automated routing (cold-standby).

Proposed configuration (initial):
- Reserved capacity: 4 x A100-class GPUs (logical sizing: 4 GPU equivalents; we’ll finalize after benchmark run).
- Isolation: dedicated node groups with single-tenant tenancy and customer VPC peering; no shared KD caches.
- Scaling: min pool = 4 GPUs, max burst = 8 GPUs for scheduled windows with 15-minute warmup policy.
- Caching: prefix and KV cache retention tuned to clinical prompt patterns (Vivek will propose TTLs).

SLA targets we should confirm:
- Uptime: 99.9% (monthly) for dedicated pool
- Latency: p95 < 150 ms (target 120ms if model quantization + batch tuning passes)
- Support: 4-hour P1 response; optional 1-hour incident escalation (enterprise add-on)

Immediate next steps & owners (actionable):
- Redwood: run 48-hour synthetic benchmark with your canonical prompt set (owner: Ben) — deliverables: latency/throughput matrix and suggested GPU sizing. ETA: 2026-07-28.
- Redwood: draft final MOP including DR steps and runbook checklist (owner: Lauren). ETA: 2026-07-26.
- MedLytics: share security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence request (owner: Alicia). ETA: 2026-07-23.
- Procurement: MedLytics procurement timeline (Tom) — share any gating dates for PO/contract.

Notes on procurement & timeline we discussed: target go-live window was early Oct; procurement wants contract + SOC2 evidence by mid-August to meet that. If procurement needs an internal SOW timeline, we can produce a committed schedule after benchmark results.

Attachment: MedLytics-MOP-draft.pdf — high-level runbook, rollback steps, and checklist.

Please reply with any corrections; Ben and Vivek will follow up with technical sizing and a short benchmark plan this week.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Redwood Inference — Inference made predictable.

From: Alicia Marino <alicia@medlytics.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + runbook: MedLytics isolation, ops MOP and SLA confirmation

Lauren —

Thanks for the thorough recap, that matches my notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- We do need EU data residency for a subset of PII datasets. Can you confirm whether the private deployment option supports regional sharding (we discussed primary us-west and a /standby/ eu-west region for those datasets)?
- For latency: the 150 ms p95 is acceptable as a baseline. If you can get us to ~120 ms after quantization that would be ideal, but we understand it depends on model and token counts.
- Warm pool: procurement is insistent on reining in costs; can you include a cost delta for keeping 1-2 warm GPUs vs fully scaling on demand?

Security team will send the SOC2 checklist to security@medlytics.com; Tom will loop in procurement with an internal schedule.

Proposed go-live target is Oct 1 — procurement has a hard freeze on budgets starting 2026-09-15, so we need DocuSign + SOC2 evidence by 2026-08-15 to be safe. I attached our internal procurement sheet (MedLytics-Procurement-timeline.xlsx).

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Marino
Head of Product Ops, MedLytics

Subject: Re: Recap + runbook: MedLytics isolation, ops MOP and SLA confirmation

Alicia / team —

Quick technical follow-up and a couple of concrete recommendations based on what we heard:

1) Autoscaling & warm pool behavior
- Recommend min=4 GPUs (reserved), warm pool of 1 GPU kept at low-util to eliminate cold-starts, burst to 8 GPUs for scheduled ingestion windows. Warm pool cost delta: approx +12-18% over pure scaling (will produce exact numbers after benchmark).

2) Quantization & model tuning
- For your clinical summarization model (70B-ish), we expect 2-3x perf improvement with 4-bit quant + kernel optimizations; actual latency gains and memory profiles will be in the benchmark report.

3) Multi-region & data residency
- We can support regional sharding at the application layer: primary inference in us-west, EU tenant for PII routing in eu-west. This requires separate dedicated pools (isolated) in each region — we should model incremental reserved capacity for eu-west only for PII workloads.

4) Reliability & SLA mechanics
- For the 99.9% target: we recommend a failover playbook (included in the MOP) with automated traffic switch to cold-standby; cold-start mitigation is a 30–60 min window unless a warm pool is held.

Attachments: sla_terms_redline.docx — I’ve flagged a handful of items (P1 response, maintenance windows, and a default rollback clause).

Next technical steps (owner / ETA):
- Benchmark plan (Ben) — run on your canonical prompt set: deliver by 2026-07-28.
- Warm-pool cost estimate and burst pricing (Ben) — deliver by 2026-07-26.
- EU region sizing draft (Vivek) — deliver by 2026-07-29.

If helpful I can hop on a short call with your procurement/security to walk through the SLA redlines next week.

—Ben
